instruction.text: Fill in the correct title for each paragraph.

atoms.b:
((What_is_a_revolution?))
A revolution is a major and lasting change that fundamentally transforms the way people live, work, and organise society, bringing about significant changes in many areas of life.

((Speed_and_extent_of_change))
Although the digital revolution has spread to almost every area of society in just a few decades, change often happens faster than society can adapt. For example, laws and education systems frequently struggle to keep up.

((Data_economy))
The digital revolution has created a new economic system in which data has become a key resource, driving the emergence of new sectors such as data analytics and artificial intelligence.

((IoT_and_big_data))
Everyday devices such as smartwatches connect to the Internet of Things (IoT), continuously collecting and sharing data. As a result, the physical and digital worlds have become closely connected. These large amounts of data can then be analysed to identify patterns, automate processes, and improve efficiency. However, big data can also be used by governments and large companies for surveillance.

((Lasting_effects))
A revolution creates lasting change. Today, schools, hospitals, businesses, and governments all depend on digital technology. Modern society could not function in the same way without it, which is why the digital revolution is considered a revolution rather than simply technological progress.

instruction.text: Read each example and decide which characteristic of the digital revolution it shows.

atoms.a: A small number of global tech companies control digital platforms that store and profit from large amounts of user data, giving them significant economic and even political power.
Smart city systems analyse traffic, weather conditions and public transport usage to automatically adjust infrastructure such as traffic lights.

Schools have introduced tablets and online learning tools, but many teachers, especially older ones, still focus on traditional teaching methods and struggle to fully integrate digital literacy into everyday teaching.
b: Internet of Things and big data

atoms.a: Many jobs now allow or require remote work using digital communication tools, a shift that has permanently changed expectations about where and how work is carried out.
b: Internet of Things and big data

atoms.a: A new social media platform becomes widely used within a few years, but legal regulations on data protection and content moderation take much longer to be developed and implemented.
Delivery vehicles collect and send real-time location data, allowing companies to optimise delivery routes and plan vehicle maintenance.
